# Source 115 — EU: AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) official policy page

- **URL:** https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai
- **Publisher:** European Commission, Digital Strategy ("Shaping Europe's digital future")
- **Published:** policy page (updated; page reflects AI Omnibus changes, prohibition 9 effective Dec 2026)
- **Type:** Official EU policy page
- **Status:** fetched 2026-09-14 (full text, http 200)

## Key claims (as stated in source)
- The **AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)** is the **first-ever comprehensive legal framework on AI worldwide**; aim: foster trustworthy AI in Europe.
- **Risk-based approach with 4 levels:**
  - **Unacceptable risk (banned):** nine prohibited practices — (1) harmful manipulation/deception, (2) harmful exploitation of vulnerabilities, (3) social scoring, (4) individual criminal-offence risk prediction, (5) untargeted scraping of internet/CCTV for facial-recognition databases, (6) emotion recognition in workplaces/education, (7) biometric categorisation to deduce protected characteristics, (8) real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement, (9) AI generating non-consensual sexually explicit/CSAM content. **Prohibitions 1–8 effective February 2025; prohibition 9 effective December 2026** (introduced via the AI Omnibus).
  - **High risk:** critical infrastructure, education, product safety components, employment/worker management, essential private/public services (e.g., credit scoring), remote biometric ID/emotion recognition/biometric categorisation, law enforcement, migration/asylum/border control, justice/democratic processes. **From 2 December 2027**, strict pre-market obligations (risk assessment, data quality, logging, documentation, deployer information, human oversight, robustness/cybersecurity/accuracy).
  - **Transparency risk:** disclosure obligations (e.g., chatbots must reveal they are AI); generative-AI providers must ensure AI-generated content is identifiable; deep fakes and public-interest text must be clearly labelled. **Transparency rules come into effect August 2026.**
  - **Minimal/no risk:** no rules (e.g., video games, spam filters).
- **GPAI models:** rules on transparency and copyright for providers; systemic-risk models must assess/mitigate risks. **GPAI rules became effective August 2025.**
- Compliance support: AI Pact (voluntary), AI Act Service Desk; July 2025 GPAI instruments (scope guidelines, GPAI Code of Practice, training-content public summary template); Code of Practice on Marking and Labelling of AI-generated content.
